name: [Portal] VOP acceptance by login: show current terms and record acceptance
description:
### Summary

When a partner opens the Partner Portal, Shoptet needs an unambiguous record that this person, acting for this partner, has accepted the terms and conditions currently in force for their language. The product decision is that acceptance happens by logging in and continuing into the portal; there is no separate confirmation control. This task delivers the partner-facing side of that decision. After a successful login, a user who has not yet accepted the current version for their language is shown the terms before any other portal page; continuing records the acceptance with user, partner, version, language and time. A user who has already accepted goes straight to the portal, and the terms stay reachable at any time from the footer and account settings. When Partnership publishes a new version in CRM, the flow runs again at the next login. Contracts, signatures and e-mail campaigns about new terms are out of scope. Depends on the CRM terms management task, the login screen and the portal shell.

### Why?

Partners must be bound by the current terms before they use portal functions such as editing their public profile or managing addons, and Shoptet must be able to prove later which wording a given person accepted and when. Partnership decided that logging in is the act of acceptance, so the portal has to make the text visible at exactly that moment rather than hiding it behind a link. Without a per-version record, publishing new terms would give no way to tell who has seen them. Keeping the terms reachable from the portal at all times is a basic legal expectation for a service partners use daily.

### What?

A partner user who logs in without an acceptance for the current terms version in their language lands on a terms page showing the full current text and a short notice that continuing into the portal means accepting it; continuing takes them to their intended destination and stores the acceptance. A user whose acceptance is already current never sees that page. A read-only terms page is linked from the portal footer and from account settings and always shows the current version with its effective-from date. When a newer version becomes effective, previously accepted users go through the page once more on their next login, and earlier acceptances remain in the record.

### Acceptance Criteria

After login, a user with no acceptance for the current version in their language is redirected to the terms page before any other portal page, including deep links; the requested destination is preserved and reached after continuing.

Continuing from the terms page stores exactly one acceptance record with portal user, partner, terms version, language and UTC timestamp; repeated logins with an unchanged version create no further records.

A user whose latest acceptance matches the current version goes straight to the portal with no interstitial.

When a newer version becomes effective for the user's language, the next login shows the terms page again and a new acceptance record is stored; older records stay untouched.

The terms page is reachable when logged in from the portal footer and from account settings, renders the current version and its effective-from date, and works in cs, sk and hu.

The terms page and the acceptance endpoint are unavailable when the 

partnerPortal

 module is inactive, consistent with the other portal pages.

New PHP passes PHPStan level 10 (

make phpstan-l10

), the acceptance decision is covered by unit tests, and the React page passes 

make fe-test

 and 

make lint

.

### Open questions

- Wiki Q7: exact surfacing — a full interstitial page before the first portal page, or a blocking notice on the overview; check whether Figma already has a screen for it.
- Legal wording of the notice that continuing constitutes acceptance; owner legal/Partnership, DevRel needs the final text in cs, sk and hu before the internal alpha.
- Whether self-registration () shows the terms before account creation, or whether the first login after registration is the acceptance moment.
- Whether acceptance is per portal user or per partner (one acceptance by any administrator covers the partner) — decides what the record means and when colleagues are asked.

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- Portal page shape to follow: `admin/controllers/PartnerPortal/PartnerPortalOverviewController.php` (`#[RequiresActiveModule('partnerPortal')]`) and `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/pages/PartnerPortalOverview/` (page.tsx, schema.ts, schema.json — Inertia typed props). The redirect gate belongs where portal controllers share a base, not in each action.
- Login: `cms/packages/Profiles/Helper/AdminUserHelper.php` (`getCrmAdminUserByCredentials` ~L300, `createAndSaveRenewHashCrm` ~L864); the login screen itself is .
- Existing consent model `st_crm.terms_consents` (`termId`, `projectId`, grantedBy/revokedBy; `cms/packages/Terms/Handlers/GrantConsentCommandHandler.php`) is per project and revocable — partner acceptance needs user + partner + version + language, so expect a new table in `database/schema/st_crm.sql` via `migrations/2026/devrel/crm/` (`migrations/AGENTS.md`).
- Current version and text come from the CRM task's query (); if that task reuses `cms/packages/Terms`, language fallback is `cms/packages/Terms/Service/FallbackTermService.php`.
- Portal user → partner record mapping is delivered by ; the acceptance record references that partner id. CODEOWNERS: PartnerPortal paths → `@shoptet/devrel-team`.
